claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The 2026 rate bound plus orthogonality implies the rate for any prescribed active set; the claim is not that special-case formula. The new optimization identifies exactly which of all active sets attains the minimax rate for every k and proves a diverging exponent ratio for the published Frobenius proxy. In particular the 2026 surrogate minimizes sum of retained squared row norms, whereas the true rate maximizes minimum retained squared row norm divided by that sum; these are different orderings. The compared published results do not state a universal surrogate optimality claim, so this is a sharp benchmark, not a refutation of such a claim.

value.rationale: Row subset selection is a motivated design problem for subspace-constrained iterative solvers. The result completely classifies the minimax choice for every size of enforced subset on a natural orthogonal-row benchmark and is simultaneously optimal at all positive finite iteration horizons. The exact three-mode family shows that the Frobenius ID surrogate, though natural for approximation, can be arbitrarily slower for expected-error convergence; this supplies a concrete diagnostic when ranking competing constraint subsets. It does not claim new generic bounds or all-purpose algorithmic superiority.
